rounds.text: Khadim India trades at a significant valuation premium with a P/E of 62.32x, which is more than double the sector benchmark of 28.87x [E6]. This high multiple is unsupported by the company's top-line performance, which shows a five-year sales growth of -10.1% [E59] and a recent year-over-year sales decline of 11% [E67]. The bottom line is also under pressure, as compounded profit growth has collapsed by 36% over the last three years and 21% over the trailing twelve months [E18, E19]. Operational efficiency is poor, evidenced by a Return on Assets of only 0.51% against a sector benchmark of 2.72% [E8]. Market sentiment appears bleak, reflected by a 0.00% dividend yield [E4] and a stock price sitting at just 9% of its 52-week range [E5]. Conceded: the company's price-to-book ratio of 1.04x is lower than the sector average [E7] and it has achieved 16% compounded profit growth over a five-year period [E17].
